claim_being_audited: The model can be certified now based on aggregate launch-readiness evidence, provided the unresolved evaluation gap for the named API migration guidance context is explicitly disclosed in the model card and audit packet.
decision_criteria: Certification must not rely on missing named-context evaluations being inferred from general benchmarks or load tests.
Material limitations and evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts must be disclosed or resolved.
A compliant certification decision requires admissible evidence of both general launch readiness and the required disclosure treatment for the unresolved named-context gap.
If the policy permits certification with explicit disclosure, the record must show that disclosure actually exists in the certification artifacts.
evidence_requests: Provide the final model-card text showing explicit disclosure of the API migration guidance evaluation gap and unknown limitation status.
Provide the audit-packet section that records the named context as an open evaluation gap rather than passed.
Provide the underlying QA statement confirming the missing evals must be treated as unknown, not passed.
Provide the launch/certification policy interpretation showing whether certification with disclosed named-context gaps is permitted, or only non-clean/provisional certification is allowed.
specific_concerns: The named deployment context has queued rather than completed evaluations, so support for certification in that context is incomplete.
The policy text requires material evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts to be disclosed or resolved before clean certification.
The actor summary asserts that disclosure will occur, but the available record does not show the actual disclosed model-card or audit-packet language.
General readiness, latency, rollback, and rehearsal evidence support launch readiness, but they do not directly establish coverage for API migration guidance.
unsupported_claims: That certification is fully supported for the named API migration guidance context.
That the required disclosure has actually been made in the model card and audit packet rather than merely recommended.
Any implication that missing eval coverage can be treated as substantively passed based on aggregate launch-readiness results.
